queries.query: Paracelsus taunting the sophists who mock his rustic Swiss birth, boasting of a hidden treasure at an inn that neither pope nor emperor could buy with all their wealth
queries.note: The polemical preface; 'rude Helvetia', 'wormy and lousy Sophist', 'monarch of arcana', and the names Leo of Rome and Charles the German paraphrased into pope and emperor; Paracelsus kept as the author's name.

queries.query: the short recipe for the philosophers' tincture: join the red essence drawn from the lion with the white gum of the eagle and thicken them by the old process
queries.note: The core prescription; 'rose-coloured blood', 'gluten', 'coagulate' paraphrased into essence, gum, thicken; the lion and eagle kept as cover-names any reader of alchemical literature knows.

queries.query: is there a single medicine that could cure every disease and prolong human life
queries.note: The tincture as Catholicum granting long life; universal-elixir claims are answered by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
